title: Deviation: MisraC2012-21.10 dependency on the hosted <time.h> implementation in rtc.c

standards_mappings.reference: Rule/directive 21.10 as written in the source annotation; normative rule text is proprietary and is not reproduced or verified by this corpus.
standards_mappings.rationale: The rule number is reproduced exactly as written in the in-source Axivion annotation at commit 308028fb. The severity classification and the normative wording of the rule are proprietary and are deliberately not asserted here.

standards_mappings.reference: SWE.4 Software Verification (static analysis evidence and justified deviance)
standards_mappings.rationale: The record is the in-source static-analysis deviance evidence for one rule set, which is part of what SWE.4 expects a project to hold. It is only partial: the repository holds no deviance log, no approval trail, no tool criticality entry for the analysing tool, and no re-analysis trigger register, so the surrounding SWE.4 evidence a qualified project would need is not evidenced at this commit.

standards_mappings.reference: Part 6 Clause 8 / Part 11 Clause 8 (coding guidelines and their justified deviations)
standards_mappings.rationale: The project states a MUST for MISRA C:2012 compatibility (docs/developer-manual/software/software-programming-language.rst:22), so these suppressions are deviations from a stated coding-guideline expectation. No ISO 26262 safety classification is claimed for any of them, and no argument is made here that the residual risk of any deviation is acceptable.

deviation_rationale: Time implementation is suitable for the application
affected_symbol: module level (whole rtc.c module body, Disable at line 70 / matching Enable at line 653)
review_disposition_note: The annotation is a block suppression: 'AXIVION Disable Style MisraC2012-21.10' is at line 70 and its matching 'AXIVION Enable Style MisraC2012-21.10' is at line 653, so the suppressed region is lines 70-653, i.e. the whole module body of rtc.c, not the single #include at line 71. The MisraC2012-1.2 pair at lines 77 and 84 is nested inside that region and is recorded separately as FB2-SW-DEV-000015; this record covers the 21.10 annotation only and makes no claim about the 1.2 pair. Governance evidence search at the pinned baseline: no deviance log, deviation log, suppression register, waiver file or review record for the MisraC2012 style checks exists anywhere in the repository (searched for *deviance*, *deviation*, *misra*, *axivion* file names and for 'AXIVION' across docs/). docs/tools/static-analysis/ and conf/spa/ do not exist at this commit. The rationale text below is therefore the only recorded justification.
reanalysis_justification: The rationale 'Time implementation is suitable for the application' is an assertion, not an argument: no property of the <time.h> implementation is named, and the claim depends entirely on which C library the TI ARM CGT runtime supplies. It is also asserted for a 584-line region (lines 70-653) that is 580 times larger than the '#include <time.h>' at line 71 that it appears to justify, so any 21.10 finding anywhere in the module is silenced by a statement written about the include alone. It must be re-analysed on any change of compiler, runtime library, or time source, and on any addition of code to rtc.c outside the include; the specific time functions actually used from <time.h> should be enumerated in the justification. The 21.10 suppression region also encloses the separate MisraC2012-1.2 Disable/Enable pair at lines 77 and 84, which is recorded on its own as FB2-SW-DEV-000015; the 'Time implementation is suitable for the application' rationale therefore does not cover the DMA-buffer section-placement code at rtc.c:77-84, and that nested site must be re-analysed under its own record.

design_traceability.coverage_note: rtc.c is not in the implementation_mapping of any as_is software design artifact; the as_is profile has no real-time-clock design element. Recorded as a coverage gap.

impact_notes.note: The include makes the RTC driver depend on a hosted C library facility; the file also runs in a freertos-plus host build for unit tests, where the implementation differs from the target one.

The RTC is the time base for timeouts and diagnostics. The suppressed check is about which time implementation is linked, which is directly safety-relevant for timeout correctness, yet the justification asserts suitability without evidence.
No as_is artifact covers the RTC driver.

The suppression is module-file-wide: it covers lines 70-653, which is 584 of the file's lines, while the rationale text is written about the single #include at line 71. Any future 21.10 finding added anywhere in rtc.c is therefore suppressed by a justification that was never written about that code, and no reviewer-visible signal distinguishes a newly silenced finding from one that was already silenced.

project_process_evidence.what_it_states: Project-level MUST: 'Code contributed to this project **MUST** be compatible with MISRA C:2012 which is described in :cite:`MISRA-C:2012`.' This is the only occurrence of 'MISRA' in the whole pinned docs/ tree and is the statement every suppression in this record set is a deviation from.

C:015 defines the project's only documented in-source deviation annotation syntax: 'If no assertion can be made for the parameter ... the parameter **MUST** be marked like this at the start of the function context: /* AXIVION Routine Generic-MissingParameterAssert: *ENTITY_NAME*: *RATIONALE* */.' The written guideline therefore mandates the '<ENTITY>: <RATIONALE>' annotation shape for one Axivion check family only; the MisraC2012 style-check family follows the same shape in practice but is not covered by any C:001..C:033 rule.

The project's own C coding guideline is a 33-rule set (C:001..C:033) with an 'Automated Check' column. Only C:002, C:004, C:005, C:006 and C:029 are marked 'Yes'; no rule in the set corresponds to a MisraC2012 style check, so the guideline set does not govern the rules these suppressions waive.

The third-party tool criticality table classifies git, TI ARM CGT, gcc, vs-code, waf, sphinx, ceedling and a custom HIL runner. No static-analysis tool (Axivion, cppcheck or equivalent) is classified, so no tool criticality or qualification basis for the tool that produced these suppressions is recorded in the repository.

corpus_scope.query: graft grep "AXIVION Disable Style MisraC2012" -i (repo root)
corpus_scope.scope_note: This set is 26 deviation records, one per (file, symbol) group, and covers all 43 'AXIVION Disable Style MisraC2012*' annotation lines found under src/ at commit 308028fb. Those 43 annotation lines fall in 20 files, and every one of the 43 is represented in the affected_lines of a record. 26 records cover 43 annotation lines over 26 distinct (file, symbol) groups because, where one symbol carries more than one MisraC2012 rule, the additional Disable lines appear as further entries in the same record's deviations array instead of as separate records. Axivion annotations outside this query are not mined by this set, and their absence must not be read as 'no deviation': 'AXIVION Routine Generic-MissingParameterAssert', 'AXIVION Next Codeline Style MisraC2012*', 'AXIVION Next Codeline Generic-LocalInclude', 'AXIVION Next Codeline CodingStyle-Naming.*', 'AXIVION Next Codeline IISB-LiteralSuffixesCheck', 'AXIVION Next Codeline Generic-NoEllipsis', 'AXIVION Next Codeline Generic-ForbiddenFunctions', 'AXIVION Routine FaultDetection-DivisionByZero', and the 'AXIVION Routine MisraC2012Directive-4.1' / 'AXIVION Routine MisraC2012-2.7' annotations. Non-MISRA families that share one of the 43 mined annotation lines ARE recorded, per record, in tool_reference.co_located_non_misra_checks and in the corresponding deviations entry (for example Generic-NoUnsafeMacro, CertC-PRE01, Generic-NoEmptyLoops, Generic-DoxygenCommentInHeader, Generic-NoMagicNumbers, IISB-LiteralSuffixesCheck); out-of-query suppression sites on the same symbol are likewise listed in the record's deviations array with a note, so that each record's rule exposure is complete for the symbol it names.
